Pin Versions Rather Than Tracking latest
A single container can consume all available memory, causing the OOM Killer to start killing processes, including host processes. Always set limits in production.

Hardcode passwords in a Dockerfile (ENV DB_PASSWORD=123): the password ends up in an image layer and is visible through docker history

Stop writes first, or use the database's native consistent-backup mechanism. Verify recovery with the service stopped, using a new empty volume or a target that has already been backed up. Extracting a tar archive overwrites files with the same names and does not automatically remove extra files from the target. The commands below demonstrate file archiving only; they do not guarantee database consistency.

<input disabled="" type="checkbox"> Does the Docker daemon expose a TCP socket? (Check Unix socket permissions; use authentication and encryption for TCP. A Unix socket is not automatically secure either.)
Does every container have --memory and --cpus limits?
Have you set a log-size limit? (daemon.json: max-size)
Does any container mount /var/run/docker.sock? (Extremely dangerous)
Are any images using the :latest tag?
Have you scanned the images with docker scout?
Additional Limits to Check Before Production

start-first and replica counts do not guarantee zero downtime: verify application readiness, connection draining, port conflicts, migrations, and cluster capacity. Non-root users, rootless mode, capabilities/seccomp, read-only mounts, and least privilege address different issues. Mounting the Docker socket expands control privileges; marking the bind mount read-only does not restrict API operations.

Standard Compose also supports file secrets. This protects how secrets are injected but does not automatically encrypt the source files. Scan results have limits in both freshness and coverage, and pinning an old digest does not automatically bring security updates. Automated prune operations need a maintenance window and must preserve rollback images; filtering by image creation time is not the same as filtering by last use.
